content:
E&O stands for errors and omissions in the delivery of professional services. For a company in the Republic of Moldova, the useful question is not simply whether a policy bearing that name can be purchased. Check whether the described activity, people, client contracts and countries of service match the proposal. A short certificate does not replace the insurance contract's conditions.

This article is a practical checklist for managers, contract staff and service-delivery teams. It does not confirm an E&O solution for every profession or determine legal liability in a dispute. Interpreting a commercial contract or claim requires a competent specialist. Insurance ING Broker SRL acts as a broker, not the insurer deciding compensation.

What should a company understand by an error or omission?

For file preparation, an error may be described as work or advice delivered incorrectly, and an omission as a necessary element left out of the service. These are indicative explanations to organise information. Read the insurer's actual definitions, the connection to alleged harm and accepted situations in the proposal. A mistake alone does not automatically establish a payable claim.

Separate redoing your own service from damage alleged by the customer. A client might request correction of a deliverable, return of a fee, reimbursement of expenses or other amounts. Ask a separate policy question about each category. Do not label them all damage without the records and explanation needed for assessment.

Describe the actual service, not only an activity code

Prepare a short account of the work performed: consulting, design, accounting, software development or another specialised service. Explain what is delivered and what falls outside the contract. Where several services are combined, describe their proportions and characteristics. A broad word such as consulting may conceal very different activities from a risk assessor.

Add an anonymised project example. Explain what information comes from the client, who approves the solution and how handover is confirmed. Do not claim the company only advises if it also administers systems or performs operations for clients. Accurate description matters more than choosing a category that appears cheaper.

Who performs the work and must be identified?

Record the contracting company, its own team and external collaborators. Explain any subcontractor's role and contractual relationship. Ask who is included in the insurance assessment and how services delivered through collaborators are treated. Paying a subcontracting invoice does not automatically include everyone in the company's policy.

For groups, check entity names and registration countries. One company may contract while another delivers. Communicate that distinction rather than hiding it in marketing material. Separate professional information needed for assessment from unrequested personal documents. A public form is not an appropriate place for complete employee files.

Read the customer's requirement before requesting a certificate

Extract the required insurance type, limit, period and special conditions from the customer contract. Seek clarification of wording that does not match the service. A professional indemnity requirement may need different assessment from general liability or cyber requirements. Do not substitute these categories simply because they appear in one commercial appendix.

Use a three-column table: customer requirement, provider response and confirming document. Mark an unaccepted condition explicitly. Do not tell the client all requirements are satisfied before comparing the final documents. A broker can explain options but cannot amend policy conditions or commercial obligations merely through an explanation.

Territory and jurisdiction are separate questions

Explain where clients are based and services used. For a Chișinău company delivering remotely, its own office does not describe the entire exposure. Identify relevant countries and dispute-resolution clauses. Request confirmation of accepted territories and jurisdictions; an English-language contract does not mean protection in every country.

This article does not interpret foreign law or recommend a court. If a customer requirement is unclear or very broad, discuss it with a legal adviser before signing. Provide its exact wording for insurance assessment, not an approximate translation. Keep answers tied to the particular contract: confirmation for one customer does not automatically extend to another.

How do project and claim timelines matter?

Arrange the service start, delivery, later changes and discovery of the problem chronologically. Ask which event and period are relevant under the insurance contract. If documents mention a retroactive date or notification period, request an explanation using your company's timeline. Do not fill those gaps by assumptions based on the E&O name.

At renewal or when changing insurers, compare continuity and any intervals without confirmed protection. A new policy does not automatically solve old work or an already known complaint. Present the actual situation and request a written response. Concealing circumstances is not an acceptable shortcut and may make an offer comparison meaningless.

Limits, deductibles and defence costs

The insurance premium is the amount paid for insurance. A deductible is the insured's own share of a loss under the contract. Also ask how the limit applies: per claim, for the whole period or in another defined way. A large figure on the first page does not explain every restriction relevant to the company.

Clarify legal expenses: when they are considered, who approves the lawyer and whether they reduce the amount available for other payments. Do not assume every legal fee the company pays is reimbursable. Compare identical activities, periods and territories. Without a common basis, a price difference may conceal a substantial difference in protection.

Exclusions and differences from other policies

Exclusions are situations the contract does not cover. Read them with definitions and endorsements, not as an isolated list. Ask about additional contractual obligations, penalties, return of your own fee, intellectual property, data and property at client premises. These are questions to check, not claims that every insurer includes or excludes them identically.

Professional liability, general liability and cyber risks are not interchangeable names. Describe the actual scenario before asking for a solution. Disputed professional advice and loss of data access following a cyber incident raise different questions. Any relationship between policies is established in their documents, not merely because both events occurred at the same firm.

Illustrative example: a disputed deliverable

A service firm completes a project, and the customer later alleges that a requested component is missing. The team gathers the accepted offer, contract version, change requests and handover confirmation. This is an editorial example, not a real client's case. It does not establish who is right or whether a policy would pay.

The project manager separates the original agreement from later requests. The company manager checks received messages and the policy notification procedure. The firm does not promise payment or admit liability on the insurer's behalf. It seeks legal advice for the dispute and sends insurance information through the indicated channel, keeping the file consistent.

What should you prepare before speaking to a broker?

  • Actual activities and deliverable types.
  • Entities, employees and subcontractors involved.
  • Client countries and relevant contractual requirements.
  • Business-size information requested in the questionnaire.
  • Representative contracts without unnecessary personal information.
  • Accurate claims history and known circumstances.
  • The existing policy, endorsements and renewal timeline.
  • Customer conditions still lacking a confirmed answer.

Keep the file useful after taking out insurance

Retain the signed policy, endorsements, application and clarifications together. Record who monitors expiry and receives activity changes. If the company moves from advice to direct operations, reopen discussion before assuming the original description remains suitable. Do the same for new services or changes in client countries.

Maintain a simple question register: subject, contact, answer, document and checking date. Distinguish a commercial explanation from an accepted contractual amendment. Without the corresponding document, mark a condition unconfirmed. This control does not guarantee avoidance of claims, but helps staff know the evidence behind client replies and renewal decisions.

Frequently asked questions about E&O in Moldova

Are E&O and professional indemnity the same?

The terms relate to professional-services risks but do not by themselves establish identical contracts. Compare activities, definitions and conditions. Clarify differences before presenting a policy as equivalent to a customer's requirement.

How much does errors and omissions insurance cost?

Your request requires assessment of activity, contracts, limits and other requested information. This article gives no confirmed rate. Compare costs after clarifying conditions and do not use a public percentage for another product as your company's quotation.

Can I send only the certificate requested by the client?

A certificate may help present insurance but does not replace review of the policy, endorsements and contractual requirements. Keep complete documents and verify that information sent to the customer matches confirmed protection.

What if a complaint has already arrived?

Preserve the timeline and records, check notification procedures and seek suitable assistance. Do not treat a new policy as a retroactive solution. Do not publish customer documents or send confidential information through an open form.
